tagline: North through the Green Swamp, where the plants catch the insects.
intro: The byway starts on NC 211 a couple of miles north of US 17 at Supply and holds to that one road all the way. The first long stretch runs almost due north through the Green Swamp, in and out of pocosins, the acid shrub bogs of the coastal plain, and out into open longleaf pine savanna. Past Bolton the road bends northwest through Clarkton and ends near Bladenboro.

This was timber and paper-mill country, and most of the land along the road is now held for conservation. The savanna stays open because it is burned on purpose. Fire keeps the woody growth down and leaves room for the small plants, and the small plants here include the Venus flytrap.

moments.title: Green Swamp Preserve
moments.text: The Venus flytrap grows wild only in a small area around Wilmington, and one of its largest wild populations is out in these wet savannas, with pitcher plants and sundews for company.

moments.title: Crusoe Island
moments.text: An isolated community on the swamp's edge by the Waccamaw River, founded in 1806 by refugees from French Haiti and home today to just a few families.

moments.title: Lake Waccamaw
moments.text: The swamp drains into Lake Waccamaw near Bolton, the largest of the oval Carolina bays, which were once blamed on meteors.
